english.title: Breach of personal licence condition - Gambling Act 2005
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..), being the holder of a personal licence issued in accordance with Part 6 of the Gambling Act 2005 and acting in the course of or in connection with any of the activities authorised by an operating licence, acted other than in accordance with the terms and conditions of the personal licence, namely **(..SPECIFY THE ACTION..)
english.legislation: Contrary to section 139(1), (2) and (4) of the Gambling Act 2005.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
being the holder of a personal licence
issued in accordance with Part 6 of the Gambling Act 2005
acted in the course of/in connection with any of the activities
authorised by the operating licence
acted other than in accordance with the terms and conditions of the personal licence

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes: Section 139(1) of the Gambling Act 2005 provides that this offence applies only where a condition attached to an operating licence includes provision for a personal licence in accordance with section 80 of the Gambling Act 2005.

other.penalty:
Fifty one weeks imprisonment and/or a fine not exceeding level five of the standard scale.

Time limit for prosecutions:
12 months

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
